sources.revision: Mutable current manual, README, and source declarations reviewed 2026-10-19; immutable commit not pinned
sources.observed: Project documentation reports broad DWG revision coverage while distinguishing stable, unstable, debugging, and unhandled classes, conditional same-version unknown-class preservation, and a list of entity/object families without test coverage. This establishes the project's own maturity distinctions, not a current independent per-family execution result.

sources.revision: Current issue pages and release listing reviewed 2026-10-19; reports remain issue-era and version-scoped
sources.observed: #123 and #124 describe single-bit mutations of locally generated AC1024 files that reportedly trigger zero-filled/capped object data, oversized allocation, or unchecked header slicing. Maintainer-linked fixes requested reporter retesting; no reporter-confirmed results for the cited controls were visible in the reviewed pages. #131 reports peer legacy code-page mapping errors. #134 reports an AC1032 MLEADER-context bounded-reader regression. These are test-shape evidence only, not ODA format authority or evidence of libdxfrw defects.

sources.revision: Mutable current documentation reviewed 2026-10-19; package artifact not run
sources.observed: The documentation distinguishes DXF entity/tag handling from cross-document XREF/import transfer and projection/rendering. Unsupported/proxy entities and selected document features are outside the documented copy route; the drawing add-on is not a 3D engine and does not render ACIS; ACIS creation requires an external library.

sources.revision: Mutable documentation/source reviewed 2026-10-19; no FreeCAD runtime or converter executed
sources.observed: DWG import composes an external converter with a selected DXF importer. The documented C++ and legacy Python importer routes have different entity subsets, and stock DXF import does not read embedded ACIS/SAT solids.

localEvidence: DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md already maps ACadRust #123/#124 to PAR-14/PAR-26 and PAR-14/7BE, #131 to the explicit code-page support/refusal policy, and #134 to the PAR-07/S8 bounded-record failure ladder.
The current plan's peer-admission and composed-evidence gates already separate declaration, typed/raw retention, writer output, strict reopen, semantic geometry, and native acceptance.
The local plan audit found no peer report that by itself establishes a new libdxfrw feature defect; exact existing test coverage must be checked before any future mutation vector is added.

assessment.planImpact: Makes per-family evidence denominators explicit, reinforces that read/retain/write/reopen/semantic/native are distinct outcomes, and supplies a safe local mutation-test recipe for relevant parser-hardening owners. Adds no duplicate local issue or peer prerequisite and does not increase routine validation cadence.

method.kind: Read current primary project documentation and public issue reports, then map the evidence to existing local plan owners
method.limitations: GitHub master/main documents and public issue pages are mutable and are not immutable executable artifacts. Reporter descriptions and maintainer-linked candidate commits were not independently reproduced. ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative for DWG byte layout; no peer report is treated as format authority or as a libdxfrw result.

implementationReadyChecks: Keep support and test denominators per format/version/family/direction/route and record source identity plus unsupported, skipped, malformed, or untested dispositions.

Before adding malformed-input coverage, inspect the exact current local selector and source path; author a valid local baseline and mutate a structurally located field rather than copying peer offsets or thresholds.
For malformed controls, assert bounded refusal, first-stage error, and no partial publication or fabricated typed contents; use a bounded child process only for a case with material allocation risk.
Keep focused target/selector/owning CTest/scoped diff as the slice gate; reserve external peers, full suites, fuzz campaigns, and native CAD for named composed checkpoints.
Preserve 2D consumers and keep explicit surfaces, modeler carriers, ACIS/AcDs association, kernel semantics, and platform-native acceptance in separate support rows.
